answer: A concrete Sybil defence is non-transferable stake bound to a proved execution identity. Each agent locks its own funds behind an enclave-signed key, and escrow rejects deposits whose funding origin already appears in the registration graph. Cloning costs the full stake again per clone instead of reusing one identity, so attack cost scales linearly while each clone's payoff stays capped by its grade; that gap is the copper floor nobody can undercut. Signed audit traces act as a trellis, letting validators prune clusters and slash stake on appeal. One timestamp anchor fixes deposit age.
